label: prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse-general
title: Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1_A — general unital R-algebra lift of [prop:t-beta-markov-frobenius-collapse]
html:
Let R be a strict-ordered field. Let A be a unital R-algebra. Let \tau : A \to R be an R-linear normalised trace (\tau(1) = 1, \tau(xy) = \tau(yx)). Let X \mapsto X^\dagger be an R-linear anti-multiplicative map on A ((XY)^\dagger = Y^\dagger X^\dagger) with 1^\dagger = 1 and \tau(X^\dagger) = \tau(X). Assume the twisted form is positive-semi-definite: 0 \le \tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) for all Y \in A. For any S \in R and X \in A satisfying \tau(X) = S:

S^2 \;\le\; \tau(X \cdot X^\dagger).

If the twisted form is non-degenerate (\tau(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = 0 \implies Y = 0), the lower bound is attained if and only if X = S \cdot 1_A.

When A is commutative, taking X^\dagger = X recovers the untwisted statement S^2 \le \tau(X \cdot X) under positivity of \tau on squares.

Relation to the substrate-model version

This proposition lifts Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1 under the canonical Markov-trace inner product on H_n(R, q) from the substrate model (A = R, \tau = \mathrm{id}) to the general unital R-algebra setting, where A may be non-commutative and infinite-dimensional.

Application to the Iwahori–Hecke algebra

For A = H_n(R, q) with \tau = \mathrm{tr}_M, take \dagger to be the R-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i. In the orthogonal seminormal form \mathrm{tr}_M(Y \cdot Y^\dagger) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \,\|Y_\lambda\|_F^2 \ge 0, so the positivity hypothesis holds. The untwisted choice \dagger = \mathrm{id} does not work for n \ge 3: \mathrm{tr}_M(X \cdot X) < 0 at X = \sigma_1\sigma_2 - \sigma_2\sigma_1 \in H_3. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the twisted form is degenerate, with radical the sum of the Wedderburn blocks of shapes with three or more rows, so the minimiser

T_\beta^{\mathrm{Markov}} \;=\; S \cdot 1_H

is unique only up to that radical. The L^2-Euclidean coordinate-norm operator and the Markov-Frobenius operator both reproduce the SDP constraint. The observable c_k Taylor coefficients remain invariant.
